architecture_principles.name: Centralized Data Protection
architecture_principles.rationale: To mitigate the risk of accidental or malicious data loss by tenant engineers, backup management must be decoupled from tenant-controlled accounts.
architecture_principles.statement: All business-critical data backups must be managed through a centralized, hardened platform account.
implications: Tenant engineers will lose direct control over backup lifecycle and encryption keys for backups.

migration_planning.sequencing_notes: Initial setup of the central governance account and SCPs is required before deploying backup plans to tenant accounts to ensure immediate immutability.

work_packages.description: Setup the dedicated central backup account and apply Service Control Policies (SCPs) to restrict tenant access.

Deploy AWS Backup plans and vaults to tenant and central accounts.

assumptions.description: AWS Organizations is used for centralized security controls across all platform accounts.
Tenant workload accounts are exclusively located in the eu-west-2 (London) region.
Tenant DevOps Engineers currently manage their own resources using Infrastructure as Code (IaC).

acceptance_criteria: Confirmation that IAM policies or SCPs prevent tenant roles from assuming 'write' permissions in the backup account.
functional_requirements.description: Implement Service Control Policies (SCPs) to restrict tenant access to the central backup account and backup configurations.

non_functional_requirements.description: The central platform must provide a backup framework using the AWS Backup Service.
acceptance_criteria: AWS Backup is configured as the central service for all backup activities.
Verification that all RDS and DynamoDB resources in scope are associated with a backup plan.
non_functional_requirements.description: Enforce a backup process across all, or selected tenants' data resources (RDS and DynamoDB).
Platform tenants should not be able to change the configuration of the backup process.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant IAM roles are unable to modify or delete AWS Backup configurations, plans, or vaults.
Production backups remain available in the local account for a minimum of 30 days.
non_functional_requirements.description: Backup data from production environments must be retained for at least 30 days within the local account.

acceptance_criteria: Non-production backups remain available in the local account for a minimum of 15 days.
non_functional_requirements.description: Backup data from non-production environments must be retained for at least 15 days within the local account.
The backup process must store copies of the backups within a separate dedicated platform-managed backup account.
acceptance_criteria: Successful automated copy of backups from tenant accounts to the dedicated backup account.
IAM policies in the backup account explicitly deny write/delete access to tenant engineer roles.
non_functional_requirements.description: Tenant Engineers must not have direct 'write' access to the dedicated backup account.

acceptance_criteria: Backups in the central account are confirmed to be encrypted with the designated CMKs.
non_functional_requirements.description: All backups within the separate dedicated account must be encrypted at rest with customer master keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS.
non_functional_requirements.target: CMK encryption for all central backups

non_functional_requirements.description: KMS keys for backups must be different from source RDS keys and inaccessible to tenants.
acceptance_criteria: KMS Key policy demonstrates that tenant engineers cannot access or schedule deletion of the backup CMKs.
A documented and tested procedure for restoring data from the central backup account to a tenant account.
non_functional_requirements.description: A restore process must be defined within the backup framework to quickly restore the data.
There should be no more than 12 hours data loss in the event a backup needs to be restored (RPO).
acceptance_criteria: Backup schedules are configured to ensure the maximum data loss window is 12 hours.

constraints.description: Management or backup of data resources other than RDS and DynamoDB is out of scope.
Implementation of the primary infrastructure or application code managed by tenant DevOps engineers is out of scope.

business_drivers.description: Need to protect business-critical data from accidental or malicious deletion.
Regulatory and compliance requirements for data retention and recovery.

architecture_vision.vision_statement: To provide a robust, automated, and tamper-proof data protection framework that ensures the recoverability of RDS and DynamoDB resources across the enterprise, independent of tenant-level administrative actions.

in_scope: Cross-account backup to a hardened central account.
Independent KMS CMK management for backups.
assumptions: AWS Organizations is the foundation for multi-account management.
constraints: Limited to RDS and DynamoDB resources only.
out_of_scope: Primary application/infrastructure code managed by tenants.

key_business_requirements.description: Centralized backup framework using AWS Backup Service.

stakeholders.name: Tenant Engineers
concerns: Maintaining autonomy while ensuring data safety.

stakeholders.name: Platform Team
concerns: Enterprise compliance, data protection, and recovery capabilities.

architecture_vision.problem_statement: Tenant DevOps Engineers have the autonomy to manage product resources, which includes the ability to delete RDS/DynamoDB instances, snapshots, and KMS keys. This flexibility introduces a critical risk of permanent data loss that cannot be mitigated within the tenant's own account boundaries.

business_goals.description: Mitigate risk of accidental or malicious data/key deletion by tenant engineers.

risks_and_mitigations.description: Accidental or malicious deletion of data resources or KMS keys by tenant engineers.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Implement a cross-account backup framework with independent encryption keys and restricted access.

risks_and_mitigations.description: Financial and reputational loss from inability to recover data.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Enforce standardized backup plans and a documented restoration process.
